evidence.wrapper_format: The downloaded file is a Java-serialized byte[] (a KAP attachment download artifact), not a raw PDF: bytes 0-22 are the serialization stream header (magic AC ED 00 05, TC_ARRAY, '[B' class descriptor, ...), bytes 23-26 are a 4-byte big-endian payload length (0x0004310A = 274698), and the PDF payload starts at byte offset 27 with '%PDF-1.7' and ends with '%%EOF', matching the declared length exactly.
evidence.identification_caveat: The per-index name on each change table is rendered as an image, not extractable text, so the table cannot be matched to 'XU030' by header text. It is identified as the BIST 30 table by document position and row-count structure: it is the first 1-added/1-removed/3-reserve table in the document, immediately followed by a 6-added/6-removed table (identified as BIST 50) and then a 27-added/27-removed table (identified as BIST 100), matching Borsa Istanbul's standard ordering (BIST 30, then BIST 50, then BIST 100) for these quarterly review documents. Caveat: the document contains at least two other 1-added/1-removed/3-reserve tables further down (each explicitly prefixed with the text label 'BIST' rather than an image), for different, unnamed sub-indices -- so the 1/1/3 row-count shape alone is not unique within the document; the BIST30 identification here relies on the combination of shape and being the first, unlabeled table at the top of the document, not on shape alone.
